capitals.note: 'his new capital, Guanggu (廣固, in modern Qingzhou, Shandong)'. Coordinates approximate.

rulers.note: Infobox: 'Titles: 350-351 King of Qi; 351-356 General Who Guards the North, Duke of Qi'; killed in 357 by Murong Jun.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: 'modern central and eastern Shandong', drawn as the whole of Shandong because the page gives no western limit. No figure for the area on the page.

region.text: 'the Shandong peninsula', Qing province, 'modern central and eastern Shandong' (Duan Qi page)

ledger.note: 350: Duan Kan founds the Qi in Shandong. 'In 350, taking advantage of the Later Zhao collapse, he occupied the Shandong peninsula and declared himself the King of Qi' at Guanggu (Qingzhou).

351: Duan Kan turns Jin's vassal. 'In 351, Duan Kan became a vassal to Jin, who appointed him the General Who Guards the North'; his title falls from King of Qi to Duke of Qi. The western-jin dossier should carry the vassal_start (counterpart duan-qi).

region.text: 'the Shandong peninsula', Qing province, 'modern central and eastern Shandong' (Duan Qi page)

ledger.note: Early 356: Murong Ke crosses the Yellow River. 'In early 356, Murong Ke's army crossed the Yellow River' and besieged Guanggu; the page says conflict between the two 'first began in 354' and Duan Kan wrote to Murong Jun in 355. The former-yan dossier dates its contest_start 355 from the Murong Jun page.

region.text: 'the Shandong peninsula', Qing province, 'modern central and eastern Shandong' (Duan Qi page)

ledger.note: 22 December 356: Guanggu surrenders. 'On 22 December 356, Duan Kan finally surrendered to Yan'.

region.text: 'the Shandong peninsula', Qing province, 'modern central and eastern Shandong' (Duan Qi page)

ledger.note: 356: Former Yan ends the Qi. 'Duan Kan's state lasted for six years before it was conquered by the Former Yan in 356'; Duan Kan, spared at first, was killed in 357 and 3,000 of his followers buried alive.

wars.name: Former Yan conquest of Duan Qi

zones.text: 'the Shandong peninsula', Qing province, 'modern central and eastern Shandong' (Duan Qi page)

wars.outcome: Murong Ke crossed the Yellow River in early 356, besieged Guanggu, and Duan Kan surrendered on 22 December 356; Shandong passed to Former Yan.
wars.note: Conflict 'first began in 354'; Duan Kan refused to recognise Murong Jun's imperial title (letter of 355).

certainty.note: A warlord state in a collapsed province: no boundary on the page; only the capital and the 'central and eastern Shandong' line.

sources.title: Duan Kan (Duan Qi)
sources.note: Whole state: 350 founding, 351 Jin vassalage, 354-356 war, 22 December 356 surrender, capital Guanggu.

sources.title: Duan tribe
sources.note: Duan Qi as a 350 offshoot of the Duan tribe, 'Duan Kan ... founded the short-lived Duan Qi state in Shandong in 350'.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; slug duan-qi, the counterpart the later-zhao (loss 350) and former-yan (contest 355-356, gain 356) dossiers already use. One page carries the whole state (the Duan Kan biography, URL Duan_Qi redirects to it); the same page reads 350 for the founding and 'early 356' for Murong Ke's crossing, one year later than former-yan's 355 contest_start. Ran Min's Wei (350-352) and Duan Qin's Zhao (352, an offshoot of the Duan tribe) are not covered here. The western-jin dossier should carry the 351 vassal_start and a vassal_end in 356.
